shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large weathered stone block
horizontal band/register line dividing the surface into upper and lower zones
repeated motifs arranged in a row along the top
incised linear/geometric detailing within the relief
justification: The most specific correspondence is the shared organisational scheme: both stones are divided by a strong horizontal band into an upper field with a row of repeated motifs and a lower field with larger profile creature forms, all in shallow relief with incised interior detail. The biggest difference is the manner of rendering — A uses sparse, recognisably naturalistic animal bodies against a plain ground, while B is filled edge to edge with dense, abstract interlocking spirals and step-fret geometry, and the block shapes (tall rectangular pillar versus squat triangular slab) differ entirely.
